stem: In which column of the statement of changes in equity is a gain on the revaluation of land entered?

options.rationale: Correct: it is an unrealised gain held in its own reserve.
Retained earnings receive profit for the year, not revaluation gains.
Share premium arises when shares are issued above par.
Share capital records the nominal value of shares.

explanation: A revaluation gain is other comprehensive income and is credited to the revaluation reserve.

stem: A company transfers US\$6,500 from retained earnings to the general reserve. What is the effect on total equity?

options.rationale: Correct: one component rises and another falls by the same amount.
The transfer moves money within equity; nothing is added.
Nothing leaves the company.
The transfer is not counted twice.

explanation: The general reserve increases and retained earnings decrease by the same amount, so the total is unchanged.

stem: Which statement about a bonus issue of shares is correct?

options.content: Cash is received from shareholders at par
options.rationale: That describes a normal issue for cash.

options.content: Total equity increases by the nominal value
options.rationale: Reserves fall by the same amount, so total equity is unchanged.

options.content: Reserves are capitalised and no cash is received
options.rationale: Correct: it is paid up from reserves.

options.content: The revaluation reserve must always be used first
options.rationale: The share premium is normally used first.

explanation: A bonus issue moves part of the reserves into share capital without bringing in cash, so total equity is the same.

stem: Retained earnings at the start of the year were US\$41,350. Profit for the year was US\$27,860, dividends declared US\$12,470 and US\$5,230 was transferred to the general reserve. What are the retained earnings at the end of the year?

options.rationale: The transfer to the general reserve has been ignored.
The dividends have been added instead of deducted.
Dividends and the transfer have both been left out.

hints: Dividends and transfers both reduce retained earnings.

stem: A company issues 16,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 nominal value at US\$1.75 each, all for cash. What amount is credited to the share premium?

options.rationale: That is the nominal value, credited to share capital.
That is the total cash received.
That is the premium on one share, not on all 16,000.

explanation: The premium is 0.75 per share on 16,000 shares = 12,000; share capital is credited with 16,000.
hints: Premium = issue price - nominal value, for each share.

stem: Which event does NOT change the total of equity?

options.rationale: A dividend reduces retained earnings and so reduces total equity.

options.content: A rights issue for cash at a premium
options.rationale: Cash is received, so equity rises.

options.content: A bonus issue from the share premium
options.rationale: Correct: reserves are converted to share capital.
A loss reduces retained earnings.

explanation: A bonus issue moves amounts between components of equity only.
hints: Does cash come in or go out?

stem: Equity at the start of the year was US\$210,800. During the year total comprehensive income was US\$51,200, dividends of US\$18,400 were paid and shares were issued for US\$36,500 in cash. What is the equity at the end of the year?

options.rationale: The cash from the share issue has been left out.
The dividend has been added instead of deducted.
Cash received from shareholders increases equity.

hints: List what increases and what decreases the owners' interest.

stem: The directors recommend a final dividend after the year end, before the statements are authorised. What is shown in the statement of changes in equity for the year just ended?

options.content: A deduction from retained earnings for the year
options.rationale: It would be deducted only if declared before the year end.

options.content: An increase in the general reserve account
options.rationale: A recommendation does not create a reserve.

options.content: A deduction from the share capital account
options.rationale: Dividends are never paid from share capital.

options.content: Nothing; the dividend is disclosed in a note
options.rationale: Correct: there was no obligation at the year end.

explanation: A dividend declared after the reporting date is a non-adjusting event; it is disclosed and recognised in the next year.
hints: Was there a liability at the reporting date?

stem: A bonus issue increases the total equity of a company.
explanation: False. A bonus issue brings in no cash. Share capital increases and the reserves used decrease by the same amount.

stem: The share premium account is a capital reserve and cannot be paid out as a dividend.
explanation: True. Share premium is capital paid in by shareholders; it can be used for a bonus issue but not for dividends.

stem: Match each event to the column of the statement of changes in equity that it changes.

left.content: Excess of issue price over nominal value
Nominal value of new shares issued for cash

explanation: Dividends reduce retained earnings; revaluation gains go to the revaluation reserve; the excess over par is share premium; the nominal value is share capital.

stem: Complete the sentence about a transfer to the general reserve.

payload.template: A transfer to the general reserve {{blank:a}} the general reserve and {{blank:b}} retained earnings by the same amount.

explanation: The transfer moves profit that has been earned from retained earnings into the general reserve.

stem: Name the column of the statement of changes in equity that records profit for the year.
explanation: Profit for the year increases retained earnings.

stem: A company has 60,000 ordinary shares of US\$2 each. It makes a bonus issue of 1 new share for every 4 held. Calculate the amount transferred from reserves to share capital.
explanation: New shares = 60,000 ÷ 4 = 15,000; amount = 15,000 × US\$2 = US\$30,000. The number of shares (15,000) is not an amount.
workedSolution: 1. New shares = 60,000 ÷ 4 = 15,000; amount = 15,000 × US\$2 = US\$30,000. The number of shares (15,000) is not an amount.

stem: Retained earnings at 1 January were US\$88,650. Profit for the year was US\$41,720. Dividends of US\$23,400 were paid and US\$9,350 was transferred to the general reserve. Calculate the retained earnings at 31 December.
hints: Both the dividends and the transfer reduce retained earnings.

stem: Share premium at the start of the year was US\$7,200. During the year the company issued 15,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 at US\$1.40 each. Calculate the share premium at the end of the year (no other movements).
explanation: New premium = 15,000 × 0.40 = 6,000; closing balance = 7,200 + 6,000 = 13,200. The new premium alone is 6,000.
workedSolution: 1. New premium = 15,000 × 0.40 = 6,000; closing balance = 7,200 + 6,000 = 13,200. The new premium alone is 6,000.
hints: The new premium is added to the old balance.

stem: Explain why a revaluation reserve cannot be used to pay a cash dividend.

points.description: The gain is unrealised: the asset has not been sold, so no cash has been received
It is a capital reserve held to show the higher value, not a profit available for distribution

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The gain on the revaluation has not been realised because the asset has not been sold, so there is no cash behind it. It is a capital reserve and not distributable profit.

explanation: One mark for unrealised or no cash and one for capital reserve.

stem: Distinguish between a bonus issue and an issue of shares for cash.

points.description: A bonus issue is paid up from reserves, but shares for cash are paid for by investors
A bonus issue brings in no cash, but an issue for cash increases the bank balance
Total equity is unchanged by a bonus issue, but it rises when shares are issued for cash

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A bonus issue is paid up from reserves and brings in no cash, so total equity stays the same. An issue for cash is paid for by investors, so cash and total equity both rise.

explanation: One mark each for source, cash and total equity.
hints: Think about where the money comes from.

stem: A company's retained earnings fell from US\$54,000 to US\$31,000 although it made a profit for the year of US\$12,000. Suggest reasons and advise the shareholders what to check.

points.description: Retained earnings fell by US\$23,000 even though profit was positive, so deductions must have exceeded US\$12,000
Possible deductions: dividends greater than profit, a transfer to a reserve, or a bonus issue paid from retained earnings
A dividend above profit uses up past profit and may weaken the company
Advice: check the statement of changes in equity for dividends and transfers, and whether the company can afford to continue

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Retained earnings fell by US\$23,000, so deductions were US\$35,000. The cause may be dividends larger than profit, a transfer to reserves or a bonus issue. Shareholders should check the statement for the amounts and whether the dividends are sustainable.

explanation: One mark for the size of the deductions, one for possible causes, one for the consequence and one for advice.

stem: Rusape Dairies Ltd had these equity balances at 1 January 2025: share capital US\$152,000 (ordinary shares of US\$1), share premium US\$12,500, general reserve US\$22,000 and retained earnings US\$47,500. In 2025 the company made a profit for the year of US\$38,640, paid a dividend of US\$16,500, issued 45,000 shares at US\$1.25 for cash and transferred US\$8,200 to the general reserve.

parts.stem: Calculate the share premium at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the retained earnings at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the total equity at 31 December 2025.
parts.explanation: Opening equity 234,000 + profit 38,640 - dividend 16,500 + cash from the issue 56,250 = 312,390. The transfer does not change the total.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Opening equity 234,000 + profit 38,640 - dividend 16,500 + cash from the issue 56,250 = 312,390. The transfer does not change the total.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the transfer to the general reserve does not change the total equity.

points.description: The general reserve increases by the amount transferred
Retained earnings decrease by the same amount, so the total is unchanged

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The general reserve rises by US\$8,000 and retained earnings fall by US\$8,000, so total equity is the same.

parts.explanation: One mark for each side of the transfer.

explanation: This item tests share premium, retained earnings and total equity in a statement of changes in equity.
